html:
A stone bridge over the Vltava river in Prague, begun in 1357 under Emperor Charles IV and finished in the early 1400s.

It replaced the older Judith Bridge, which a flood had swept away in 1342. The architect was Peter Parler, who also worked on Saint Vitus Cathedral. The bridge joined the Old Town with the castle side of the city, and for more than four centuries it was the only fixed crossing of the river in Prague.

Charles made Prague the capital of the Holy Roman Empire and founded its university in 1348. The bridge was part of that building boom. In the 1600s and 1700s it gained a row of Baroque statues of saints, among them John of Nepomuk, who was thrown from the bridge in 1393. Today it carries only people on foot and is one of the most visited places in Europe.
sum: A stone bridge over the Vltava river in Prague, begun in 1357 under Emperor Charles IV and finished in the early 1400s.
